papers.title: Bound states at Trudinger--Moser growth: obstructions, pairing and bubbling
papers.abstract: We study radial solutions of the planar scalar field equation $$ -\Delta u+u=\lambda u\,e^{u^2}, \qquad 0<\lambda<1, $$ whose nonlinearity has critical Trudinger--Moser growth. These solutions describe standing waves of the two-dimensional nonlinear Schr\"odinger and Klein--Gordon equations. Motivated by Tang's recent uniqueness result for radial bound states with power nonlinearities in higher dimensions, we investigate the validity of the corresponding uniqueness theory at critical exponential growth. We show that the Serrin--Tang criterion and two structural hypotheses in Tang's analysis fail in this setting. We establish a pairing principle for the shooting problem, prove that Tang's variation conditions force the nodal count to be non-decreasing, and show that any two radial ground states intersect. We also derive a second-order expansion of the Liouville bubble arising at large initial heights and compute the corresponding flux correction. These asymptotics yield formal predictions for the first zero and the nodal structure at large heights. Our results suggest that the ground state is unique, whereas nodal radial bound states, if they exist, occur in pairs, contrary to the uniqueness phenomenon for power nonlinearities.

papers.title: Fundamental solutions to Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck equations with unbounded lower order terms
papers.abstract: We continue the study of fundamental solutions for equations involving Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck operators with rough local or non-local diffusions. Here we consider possibly unbounded lower order terms, such as drifts and potentials. We prove existence and uniqueness of weak solutions and of an appropriate notion of fundamental solution for a wide class of kinetic equations. This is based on kinetic transfer of regularity and anisotropic embeddings.

papers.title: The kinetic Kato square root problem
papers.abstract: We solve the kinetic Kato square root problem for the whole-space Kolmogorov operator $$H_A=\partial_t-X\cdot\nabla_Y-\operatorname{div}_X(A\nabla_X)$$ on \(\mathrm L^2\) with Lebesgue measure, where \(A\) is a bounded measurable complex uniformly accretive matrix depending on all variables. We define its realization through a sesquilinear form and identify the square-root domains of the resulting maximal accretive operator and its adjoint with the intrinsic Sobolev space defined by one velocity derivative and half a derivative along the transport flow. The homogeneous norm equivalences depend only on the dimension and the coefficient bounds. The energy also controls a position derivative of order one third. The proof uses second-order resolvents and localized affine testing. A regularized transport symmetrizer gives hidden coercivity, while comparison with a positive Rockland operator supplies intrinsic smoothing. Commutator and dyadic approximation estimates remove the smoothing before a Carleson argument is applied. We also obtain uniform shifted square-root estimates and bounded velocity, transport and position Riesz transforms.

papers.title: A Note on Fractional Sobolev inequalities revisited
papers.abstract: In this paper, we extend the analysis of homogeneous fractional Sobolev inequalities in the paper by A.D. Nguyen, J. I. D{\i}az, and Q.-H. Nguyen (2020). We combine their subcritical proof with the first author's adaptation to the supercritical case to provide a short interpolation-based proof for the critical case.

papers.title: Critical orthonormal Strichartz estimates for Lebesgue spaces
papers.abstract: We study orthonormal Strichartz estimates at the critical coefficient exponent $q/2$ for fractional Schr\"odinger propagators. The proof for $d\geq3$ combines annular Schatten estimates with a frequency summation argument based on potential duality and Littlewood--Paley theory. In dimension two, a trace computation supplies the annular estimate needed for the global estimate. We also construct a counterexample to the global estimate with spatial $L^\infty$ and coefficients in $\ell^{q/2}$, even with a weak time norm.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the Jacobian Conjecture from the viewpoint of lineability
papers.abstract: Algebraic genericity in the family of polynomial counterexamples to the recently solved Jacobian Conjecture for $N\ge3$ is investigated. The notion of affine-coneability is introduced and it is shown that this family is affine-coneable and 1-lineable, but not 2-lineable. Semigroupability is further studied with respect to coordinatewise multiplication and composition.

papers.title: Convergence of non-symmetric forms with changing reference measures
papers.abstract: We develop a functional-analytic theory of convergence for non-symmetric generalized Dirichlet forms defined on a sequence of Hilbert spaces $H_n$ converging to a limit space $H$ in the sense of Kuwae-Shioya, with the principal applications concerning $L^2$-spaces over varying reference measures $\mu_n \to \mu$. Extending Mosco's variational convergence for Dirichlet forms to the non-symmetric setting via a functional controlling the off diagonal values of the forms, we introduce a notion of generalized convergence of non-symmetric Dirichlet forms and show it to be equivalent to strong convergence of the associated resolvents, to weak convergence of the co-resolvents, and to strong graph convergence of the infinitesimal generators. A version of the Trotter-Kato theorem in the Kuwae-Shioya framework yields the corresponding equivalence for $C_0$-contraction semigroups. As applications, we give sufficient conditions for the generalized convergence of elliptic and sectorial $a_{i,j}$-forms with changing speed measures, both on $\mathbb{R}^d$ and in infinite dimensions over a Gelfand triple, and deduce weak convergence of the laws of the associated right processes under tightness of the path measures.

papers.title: Operator Fej\'{e}r--Riesz Theorems with Gaps and Degree Bounds
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a nonempty compact semialgebraic subset of the real line, and let $S$ be a saturated scalar description of $K$. We prove that every hermitian polynomial with bounded-operator coefficients that is positive semidefinite on $K$ belongs to the operator quadratic module generated by $S$. We also show that if such a polynomial has degree at most $\tt{d}$, then it admits a certificate of weighted degree at most $\tt{d}+c_S$, where $c_S$ depends only on $S$, not on the polynomial or the coefficient Hilbert space. In contrast to the scalar case, where natural preorderings admit the degree bound $\tt{d}$ independently of $K$, we show that no uniform additive constant exists for natural matrix preorderings. We construct quadratic $2\times2$ matrix polynomials positive semidefinite on unions of two intervals whose minimum certificate degrees in the corresponding natural preorderings diverge as one interval shrinks to a point, while the gap length remains bounded below. Conversely, we establish uniform bounds of the form $\tt{d}+C$ for families of interval unions contained in a fixed compact interval when interval lengths and gap lengths have uniform positive lower bounds. Our proofs develop two techniques that may be of independent interest. First, a quadratic reduction principle represents arbitrary-degree operator polynomials as compressions of quadratic ones on enlarged Hilbert spaces. A perturbation argument and the closedness of truncated operator quadratic modules then extend uniform degree bounds from the quadratic case to arbitrary degrees with linear degree bounds of slope $1$. Second, a rank-one symmetric matrix pencil transfers positivity on interval unions to $[0,1]$, where the operator Fej\'er--Riesz theorem yields certificates.

papers.title: A height transportation approach to the quantitative Pr\'ekopa--Leindler inequality
papers.abstract: We give a new, simpler proof of sharp stability for the Pr\'ekopa--Leindler inequality. In contrast to the main arguments from Figalli, van Hintum and Tiba~\cite{FigalliVanHintumTibaPL}, our proof hinges mostly on the sharp stability theory for the Brunn--Minkowski problem, developed by the same authors \cite{figalli2024BM}, and on the idea of using a height transportation approach in order to match level sets. As a by-product of our techniques, we are able to prove the sharp dependency on $\tau = \min\{\lambda,1-\lambda\}$ in the Pr\'ekopa--Leindler stability constant whenever one of the inputs is logarithmically concave, producing a new, simplified proof of two of the main results from~\cite{FigalliVanHintumTibaPL}. Finally, in the same fashion as Krist\'aly and P\^irvuceanu \cite{kristaly2026quantitative}, we are able to obtain new stability results for the Bakry-Emery log-Sobolev inequality and for the Talagrand inequality. Due to the sharpness of the inputs, these results are optimal in terms of exponents. We moreover show that the $L^1$ nature of the distance in such results \emph{cannot} in general be improved to any other $L^p$ distance, where $p>1.$

papers.title: Order continuity of induced homomorphisms between free Banach lattices
papers.abstract: Let $T\colon F\to E$ be a bounded operator between Banach spaces and let $\overline T\colon FBL^{(p)}[F]\to FBL^{(p)}[E]$ be the lattice homomorphism induced by $T$ between the corresponding free $p$-convex Banach lattices generated by $F$ and $E$. We show that $\overline T$ is order continuous if and only if it is either zero or a lattice isomorphic embedding. For $p=\infty$, this holds precisely when $T$ is zero or an isomorphic embedding, while for $1\leq p<\infty$, apart from the zero operator, $T$ must be an embedding and the pair $(T(F),E)$ must have the operator-extension property POE-$p$. In addition, we study when $FBL^{(p)}[E]$ is order dense or majorizing in $FBL^{(q)}[E]$ for $p<q$.

papers.title: Clarkson--McCarthy type inequalities, part II: refinements, unitary orbits, unitarily invariant norms and $\ell_s$--$\ell_s$ estimates
papers.abstract: In previous work \cite{Zha26a}, the author established Clarkson--McCarthy type inequalities for several classes of operator families, including $\ell_p$--$\ell_p$ estimates and mixed $\ell_q$--$\ell_p$ estimates, by means of operator square-sum identities. The present paper has two main aims. First, using the tracial joint spectral measures recently introduced by O.~Hein\"avaara \cite{Hei25}, we obtain several refinements of the McCarthy--Clarkson inequalities, one of which confirms a conjecture of Audenaert \cite{AK17}. Second, combining tools from matrix analysis with complex interpolation theory, we establish Clarkson--McCarthy type inequalities for unitary orbits, unitarily invariant norms, and $\ell_s$--$\ell_s$ estimates, again in the framework of operator square-sum identities.

papers.title: Continuous, locally Lipschitz and Lipschitz selections for intuitionistic fuzzy sets, with applications to expert voting
papers.abstract:
This paper studies continuous selections in the framework of intuitionistic fuzzy sets. To each intuitionistic fuzzy set $A=(\mu,
u)$ on a topological space $X$ we associate the interval-valued map $F_{A}(x)=[\mu(x),1-
u(x)]$, whose width is the hesitation degree. Hence, in this setting, a selection of $F_{A}$ is an ordinary fuzzy membership function compatible with the intuitionistic information, and every selection is the membership function of Atanassov's operator $D_{\vartheta}$ for a suitable pointwise parameter $\vartheta$. When $X$ is normal and $\mu$, $
u$ are upper semi-continuous, a continuous selection exists by the Kat\v{e}tov--Tong insertion theorem. We show that upper semi-continuity arises naturally in a voting model, in which a panel of experts divides a metric universe into closed regions of acceptance and rejection, and for this model we construct an explicit continuous selection, the consensus selection, illustrated by a non-compact example in the plane. On metric spaces we characterise the intuitionistic fuzzy sets that admit an $L$-Lipschitz selection through a non-local version of the condition $\mu+
u\leq 1$, and we give the largest and the smallest such selections in closed form. Finally, we prove that the set of continuous selections depends in a $1$-Lipschitz way on the intuitionistic fuzzy set, with respect to the Hausdorff-type distance of Grzegorzewski. We also characterise the intuitionistic fuzzy sets admitting locally Lipschitz selections.

papers.title: A new perspective on Riemann surfaces and von Neumann algebras via thin Blaschke products
papers.abstract: In 2014, K.Guo and the second author constructed the first example of an infinite Blaschke product $B$ (a thin Blaschke product), for which the associated multiplication operator $M_B$ is irreducible on the Bergman space $L_a^2(\mathbb{D})$ over the unit disk $\mathbb D$. We take a substantial step forward toward characterizing the irreducibility of the operator $M_B$ on $L_a^2(\mathbb{D})$, or equivalently, the trivialness of the von Neumann algebra $\{M_B,M_B^*\}'$. This characterization indicates a close connection with the primeness of $B$ and with the two-component property of the Riemann surface $\mathcal{S}_B$ associated with $B$. The approach is built upon a nested family of connected components of the sublevel set $\{z\in \mathbb{D}:|B(z)|<t\}$ for $0<t<1$, which captures the function-theoretic and geometric feature of $B$.

papers.title: Functions of $\boldsymbol{S}_p$-almost commuting unitary operators and contractions. An extension of the Carey--Pincus trace formula
papers.abstract: In this paper we study functions of pairs of unitary operators and pairs of contractions with commutators in the Schatten-von Neumann class $\boldsymbol{S}_p$. We obtain commutator estimates and prove that our functional calculus is multiplicative modulo $\boldsymbol{S}_p$. On the other hand, we show that our commutator estimates do not extend to the case $p>2$. We also obtain an extension of the Carey--Pincus trace formula. The main tool of this paper is a technique of triple operator integrals.

papers.title: Linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant. III
papers.abstract: This paper is the third in the series of papers devoted to the explicit description of linear maps preserving the Cullis' determinant of rectangular matrices of size $n\times k$ with entries belonging to an arbitrary ground field which is large enough. In this part we study the remaining case where $k = 3$ and $n \ge k + 2 = 5$ and prove that every linear map preserving the Cullis' determinant admits the same description as for the case where $k \ge 4$ and $n \ge k + 2$ obtained previously.

papers.title: Counterexamples to uniqueness for a discrete X-ray transform under quadratic decay
papers.abstract: We show nonuniqueness for a discrete X-ray transform on $\mathbb Z^2$ under quadratic decay. We construct an explicit nonzero function in $\ell^1(\mathbb Z^2)$ with pointwise decay $O(|z|^{-2})$ whose sums over integer lines vanish. We also obtain an infinite-dimensional null space with the same decay assumption. Furthermore, we show a result which indicates that the decay rate $|z|^{-2}$ may be sharp and faster decay may imply uniqueness.

papers.title: Similarity cancellation and primitive operator roots
papers.abstract: Kaplansky's second test problem for similarity asks whether $A\oplus A\sim B\oplus B$ implies $A\sim B$ for bounded operators on a separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. We answer this question in the negative, even for compact operators whose singular values satisfy any prescribed positive upper bounds tending to zero. We also show that cancellation can fail under the stronger hypothesis $J_2(T)\sim J_2(S)$ considered by Marcoux, Radjavi, Troscheit, and Zhang \cite{MRTZ}. For these operators, finite amplifications and primitive roots are similar exactly at even multiplicities and even orders, respectively. In contrast, cancellation in fixed matrix size admits a uniform bound on the condition number. This extends the finite type~$I$ results of Jiang, Ma, Shi, and Zhang \cite{JMSZ}. The bound also holds for simultaneous similarity of arbitrary families of matrices and can be chosen to tend to one as the amplified bound tends to one. We conclude that, in a finite type~$I$ von Neumann algebra, cancellation of doubles and cancellation of primitive square roots are each equivalent to boundedness of the orders of its nonzero homogeneous summands.

papers.title: Optimal lengths of commutators of idempotents and similarity of nilpotent operators to their negatives
papers.abstract: Let $\HH$ be a complex separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert space. We prove that every operator in $\BH$ is a sum of three commutators of idempotents and a product of two such commutators. Both numbers are best possible. The same is true for differences of idempotents, for operators similar to their negatives, and for operators anticommuting with an involution. Each of these four classes therefore has additive length three and multiplicative length two. We also construct nilpotent operators of order three that are similar to their negatives but cannot be conjugated to their negatives by any bounded involution. These results answer Question~7.22(a)--(c), the question in Remark~7.17, and the question about involutions in Section~2.9 of Marcoux, Radjavi and Zhang, \emph{J. Funct. Anal.} \textbf{284} (2023), 109854.

papers.title: The sharp Stein-Tomas inequality on the circle
papers.abstract: We prove that constant functions are global maximizers for the endpoint Stein--Tomas inequality on $\mathbb{S}^1$, thereby determining its sharp constant. By the known characterization of the phases of maximizers, every nonzero maximizer then has the form $f(\omega)=c e^{ix_0\cdot\omega}$, where $c\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}$ and $x_0\in\mathbb{R}^2$.

papers.title: A short proof of the complete Crouzeix inequality in dimension three
papers.abstract: We give a short proof of the complete Crouzeix inequality with sharp constant $2$ for matrices of dimension at most three.

papers.title: The Marvelous Meixner Polynomials: Second Kind, First Class
papers.abstract: Meixner's classification asks which exponential generating functions can generate orthogonal polynomials. We follow the continuous Meixner family from this question to its moments, measures, and continued fractions. A beta integral and a bilinear identity establish positivity and orthogonality; Carlitz's Bernoulli and Euler constructions reveal further connections. Turning the parameter into a variable leads to rational orthogonality and Wall's fraction. We derive its Nevanlinna measure and unite the two spectral directions in a joint law with Cauchy marginals. Even finite pencils produce couplings with these exact marginals. Laguerre limits explain the gamma law governing joint extremes. Along the way, Meixner's scientific life, combinatorics, tangent numbers, and even zeta values illuminate the same structure.

papers.title: The ball fixed point property for continuous functions on locally compact spaces
papers.abstract: Let $K$ be a compact Hausdorff space and $p\in K$. We prove that the Banach space $C(K,p)=\{f\in C(K,\mathbb R):f(p)=0\}$ fails the ball fixed point property (BFPP) whenever $p$ is non-isolated, answering a question of Avil\'es, Jap\'on, Lennard, Mart\'inez-Cervantes and Stawski. Consequently, $C_0(L)$ fails the BFPP for every noncompact locally compact Hausdorff space $L$. Together with Barroso's characterization for $C(K)$, this yields complete topological classifications of the BFPP for $C_0(L)$ and $C(K,p)$. We also resolve a second question of Avil\'es et al., showing that the BFPP of $C(K)$ implies that of $C(K,p)$ for every compact Hausdorff space $K$ and every $P$-point $p\in K$ if and only if there are no measurable cardinals.

papers.title: A general framework for universal bounds on the analytic functional calculus
papers.abstract: We establish a general principle for bounding the matrix-valued analytic functional calculus $F\mapsto F(T)$ of a Hilbert space operator $T$, independently of the matrix size. It rests on two properties of an auxiliary Hilbert space of holomorphic functions: the accretivity of its moment map at $T$ and a uniform bound for its multipliers. The mechanism of OpenAI's direct proof of the complete Crouzeix conjecture is the instance in which these properties come from the positivity of the double-layer potential and from norm estimates for Faber series of a convex domain. The main advantage of our method is that the auxiliary space can be chosen freely, to fit the class of operators, and a well-chosen space can give sharp constants, also on domains that are not convex, simply connected or bounded. On every intersection of two disks of the Riemann sphere, for operators with both closed disks as spectral sets, we obtain a complete bound independent of the two disks, which is sharp for the quantum annulus and the strip. For operators, bounded or m-sectorial, with numerical range in a sector, our bounds improve on the complete Crouzeix inequality for every opening; they are optimal for the right angle, answering a question of Crouzeix, and nearly optimal for acute angles. On Jordan domains with regular real-analytic boundary, a space built from the exterior conformal map and the Faber polynomials of the domain gives complete bounds for operators whose double-layer potential is bounded below. They are optimal for the disk, recover the complete Crouzeix inequality on convex domains, and improve on earlier bounds, including bounds of Crouzeix and Greenbaum, also on nonconvex domains.

papers.title: Alternating chains and lattice strict singularity
papers.abstract: We present an alternating-chain argument intended to show that every lattice strictly singular operator from a real Banach lattice to a real Banach space is disjointly strictly singular. A hypothetical counterexample yields two LSS operators on a reflexive sequence lattice whose difference is bounded below. Quotienting by the range of that difference gives a common map bounded below on a positive tail cone. Finite chains of positive disjoint vectors, with alternating small differences, then lead to incompatible length estimates. We record the resulting operator and sequence consequences and extend the construction to common postcompositions with DSS errors. Independently of the proposed equality, we prove simultaneous nuclear restriction results for countable DSS families and uniform nuclear tails for norm-compact DSS families, together with common Hilbert-space factors and arbitrarily small nuclear corrections having a common infinite-dimensional kernel. Examples identify limits of these selection statements. The main equality is a candidate real-field proof; no complex-field equality is asserted.

papers.title: Transfer of similarity to Hilbert space contractions through inner functions: a proof of Douglas's conjecture
papers.abstract: Let $A$ be a bounded operator on a Hilbert space and let $u$ be a non-constant Blaschke product, finite or infinite. We prove that if the spectrum of $A$ does not meet the closure of the set of poles of $u$, then $u(A)$ is similar to a contraction if and only if $A$ is. This settles a conjecture of R.G. Douglas. For infinite products $u$, no additional condition on the zeros beyond the Blaschke condition is required. We also show that '$u(A)$ is similar to a contraction if and only if $A$ is' for all non-constant inner functions $u$ whose reflected singularity set, the closure of the set of poles together with the singular support, avoids the spectrum of $A$. We also prove a weighted resolvent version of the theorem, which allows the poles to accumulate on the spectrum to a limited extent; a column criterion for partial products, which is shown to force their norm convergence; and a simultaneous version for commuting tuples of operators tested by separated inner functions sharing one Lyapunov operator. For finite Blaschke products we obtain a polynomial form of the Lyapunov operator, which gives an estimate for the similarity constants. We also characterise the tuples of finite Blaschke products that form a uniform strong test collection: they are exactly the tuples that are injective, with non-vanishing joint derivative, on the closed disc. Finally, we show by examples that the separation hypothesis cannot be replaced by the existence of a bounded $H^\infty$ calculus, by the existence of a norm radial limit, or by the strong convergence of the partial products, even for Ritt operators.

papers.title: Algebraic properties of Toeplitz operators on annulus and multiply connected domains
papers.abstract: We study the Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space over the annulus and provide a complete characterization of them. Based on that, we single out a certain class of Toeplitz operators that satisfy the multiplicativity property and lead to a zero product theorem. We further extend the results for the general multiply-connected domain and prove the zero product theorem for Toeplitz operators on the Hardy space over such a domain.

papers.title: Improved Berezin--Li--Yau Bounds for Dirichlet Eigenvalues via Fourier Coupling and Frequency Concentration
papers.abstract: Let $0<\lambda_1\leq\lambda_2\leq\cdots$ be the Dirichlet eigenvalues of an open set $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$. We develop two Fourier-space refinements of the Berezin--Li--Yau argument. For every finite-measure open set, coordinate commutator identities and coupled scalar--vector projections lead to a one-dimensional variational constant $C_n^{\mathrm{new}}$ and the individual bound \[ \lambda_k\geq C_n^{\mathrm{new}}(2\pi)^2\omega_n^{-2/n} |\Omega|^{-2/n}k^{2/n}, \qquad \frac{n}{n+2}<c_n^{\mathrm{env}}<C_n^{\mathrm{new}}<1. \] Here $n/(n+2)$ is the classical Li--Yau individual coefficient and $c_n^{\mathrm{env}}$ is the coefficient associated with the uncoupled scalar envelope developed in our previous paper. Thus the displayed strict hierarchy separates the gain of the scalar energy envelope from the further gain supplied by the commutator coupling. For bounded open sets, a frequency-concentration operator, its first two traces, and the Ky Fan principle force Fourier mass outside the Li--Yau filling ball. A two-region bathtub argument then gives \[ \sum_{j=1}^k\lambda_j \geq \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(\Omega) \frac{n}{n+2}(2\pi)^2\omega_n^{-2/n} |\Omega|^{-2/n}k^{1+2/n}, \qquad \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(\Omega)>1, \] where $\mathcal C_k^{(2)}(\Omega)$ is strictly decreasing in $k$ and converges to one, and \[ \mathcal C_k^{(2)}(\Omega)-1\geq \frac{n+2}{2(n+1)^2} \left(\frac{\omega_{n-1}}{\omega_n}\right)^2 \left(\frac34\right)^{n-1}k^{-2/n}. \] Thus the sharp leading term in the Berezin--Li--Yau sum is supplemented by an explicit positive, volume-only correction of order $k$. Apart from boundedness in the concentration argument, no boundary regularity, convexity, or connectedness is assumed. These improvements do not prove P\'{o}lya's conjecture: the individual coefficient is below one, and the sum multiplier tends to one.

papers.title: Carleson Measures and Integral Operators on Fock--Sobolev Spaces
papers.abstract: For integers $n\ge1$ and $N\ge0$, let $\mathbf g=(g_0,\ldots,g_N)$ be a vector of entire functions. We consider the generalized integral operator \ [T_{\mathbf g}^{(n,N)}f =I^n\!\left(\sum_{j=0}^N g_jf^{(j)}\right), \qquad (Ih)(z)=\int_0^z h(w)\dd w. \] We characterize its boundedness and compactness between Fock--Sobolev spaces $\F_m^p$ and $\F_\ell^q$, where $0<p,q<\infty$ and $m,\ell\ge0$ are integers. The coefficients of critical total degree determine the operator modulo compact operators and yield essential-norm estimates. In the Hilbert case, a Laurent Toeplitz representation gives the exact essential norm, a Fredholm criterion and an index formula. As an application, we obtain conditions for solutions of linear differential equations to belong to Fock--Sobolev spaces, including a necessary and sufficient polynomial zero condition in the Hilbert case. For entire functions $u_0,\ldots,u_N$ and $\varphi$, we also characterize boundedness, compactness and essential norms of the operators \[ L_{\mathbf u,\varphi}^{(N)}f =\sum_{j=0}^N u_j\,f^{(j)}\circ\varphi. \] The proofs use Carleson measure characterizations for finite sums of weighted differentiation operators on Fock--Sobolev spaces.

papers.title: Tensor Products and the Isomorphic Theory of Daugavet Spaces
papers.abstract: We construct two separable Banach spaces with the Daugavet property whose injective and projective tensor squares, respectively, fail the Daugavet property. Both examples arise from one sequence of finite-dimensional extensions. The first space is the completion of the increasing union of the extensions, whereas the second is the closed span of their coordinate functionals. We will also investigate the operator Daugavet properties of these spaces later in the paper, also highlighting natural examples of metric spaces \(M\) for which \(\operatorname{Lip}_0(M)\) has the Daugavet property but fails to have the weak operator Daugavet property. Independently of this, we will also prove that every Banach space admits a linear isometric embedding into a Banach space which is not isomorphic to any Banach space with the Daugavet property.

papers.title: Sobolev spaces arising from the Stockwell transform on Gelfand pairs
papers.abstract: We introduce a family of Sobolev-type spaces on Gelfand pairs, built from the Stockwell transform: a function belongs to the space of a given smoothness when its Stockwell transform, multiplied by a weight that grows with the smoothness, is square integrable. We prove that these spaces are Hilbert spaces, that they form a decreasing scale under continuous embeddings, and that an interpolation inequality controls the norm at an intermediate smoothness by the norms at the two endpoints. Under integrability conditions on the weight and on the family of analysing windows, they embed continuously into Lebesgue spaces. Under a local domination condition on the window, we show that their elements have bounded continuous representatives. On the Euclidean motion group, where the Stockwell transform reduces to a windowed Hankel transform, this gives boundedness and continuity as soon as the smoothness exceeds half the dimension, which is the classical threshold for Euclidean spaces.
